examples.before: .troupe/troupe.yml has short keys (`name: demo`, `retry: 3`) next to `very_long_setting_name_here: some fairly long value text`

results.1: exit 0; every note sits one space after its value, with no column alignment: `name: demo # from .troupe/troupe.yml`, `very_long_setting_name_here: some fairly long value text # from .troupe/troupe.yml`
results.2: same output as route 1: one space before each `#`, no alignment

examples.before: agents.coder points to agents/coder.yaml (`model: sonnet`, `system_prompt_identifier: "x: y"`); agents.note points to prompt.txt (two lines)

results.1: exit 0; `  model: sonnet # from .troupe/agents/coder.yaml`, `  system_prompt_identifier: 'x: y' # from ...`, `note: | # from .troupe/prompt.txt` with the two text lines below it and no note on them
exit 0; `- opus # from .troupe/troupe.yml` / `- a-much-longer-model-name-entry # from .troupe/troupe.yml`, no alignment

context.in_practice: Every arm on both routes printed the notes one space after the value, with no lining up. So route 2 made the same choice as route 1 without considering it, and nothing a user sees tells the two apart here. Neither route ever lined the notes up in a column.
context.stakes: How easy `config show --sources` output is to scan: whether the `# from <file>` notes sit one space after each value or line up in a column. In these runs the output was identical on both routes, byte for byte.
context.tradeoff: Route 1: a stated, predictable rule, but notes are ragged when key and value lengths vary. Route 2: the same output with no stated reason behind it.

plan_why: Shows where `show --sources` puts `# from <file>` comments when lines have different lengths: one space before `#` with no alignment, or some other spacing such as a fixed column, two spaces, or padding. Covers nested mappings, list items, flow-quoted strings, includes and a multi-line text include.
